standard_prerequisites.name: Evans's construction of *-generic structures from a class C_f with predimension, and the criteria for the generic to be well-defined and simple
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 1758-1766; the individual amalgamation check follows Remark 3.8 of the cited Evans paper
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the theory S_n and justifies that the generic exists and is simple even though the criteria hold only for x >= n+2.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relation between SU-rank, non-minimality degree and predimension in this setting
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 1769-1771 and 1778-1781
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the rank computation and the predimension estimates into the two bounds nmdeg(p) <= n and nmdeg(p) >= n.

core_obligations: Choose the data: a single k-ary relation with k = n+1, the predimension delta(A) = 2|A| - |R(A)|/k!, and the piecewise f that equals 2x-2 up to n+2 and then continues logarithmically (proof lines 1758-1761).

Justify well-definedness: the simplicity criteria hold only for x >= n+2, but the finitely many amalgamation instances involving structures of size at most n+1 are checked individually - those structures either carry no relation or carry exactly one - so the generic is well-defined and simple (proof lines 1764-1769).

Upper bound: since f(x) >= 2 for x >= k there is a unique 1-type p, and since f(x) <= 2x-1 for x <= k the theory has a k-element structure with exactly one instance of R, so SU(p) = 2 and nmdeg(p) <= k-1 = n (proof lines 1769-1771).

Lower bound: distinct a_1, ..., a_n have a unique type, because the predimension bound forces the algebraic closure to have size at most n+1 and size exactly n+1 is impossible as the least predimension of an (n+1)-element set is 2n+1 > 2n = d_0(a_1...a_n) (proof lines 1773-1781).

Strict inequality: for a non-constant indiscernible sequence either every (n+1)-tuple satisfies R - impossible since long such sequences have negative predimension - or none does, in which case the predimension and closure estimates give a_{n+1} independent from a_1, ..., a_n and hence F_ind(p) > n (proof lines 1806-1814).
proof_roadmap: Instantiate Evans's construction with a piecewise f and check the finitely many amalgamation instances to keep the generic simple (proof lines 1758-1769).
Compute nmdeg(p) = n from the rank and two predimension estimates, then show F_ind(p) > n through the indiscernible-sequence analysis (proof lines 1769-1814).
difficulty_reason: The theorem exhibits, for every n, an omega-categorical supersimple theory with a type whose fibre dimension strictly exceeds its non-minimality degree, the degree being exactly n (statement lines 1749-1754). The proof instantiates the same generic construction as the earlier existence result but with a piecewise f whose simplicity criteria only hold from n+2 onwards, so the finitely many amalgamation instances involving small structures have to be checked individually following the cited remark (proof lines 1758-1769). The two steps that carry the content are then the computation nmdeg(p) = n, which combines the rank with a predimension obstruction to the algebraic closure of n points having size n+1, and the strict inequality F_ind(p) > n, where the indiscernible-sequence analysis splits into the case where all (n+1)-tuples satisfy the relation - impossible because long sequences would have negative predimension - and the case where none does (proof lines 1769-1814). Both estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the proof. H2.
